The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN) is working on a program that would create new restrictions on the companies offering WHOIS privacy services, or “Providers.” Under the proposed new rules, Providers would be required to monitor your use of domain names and websites. Providers could be forced to terminate your privacy service and be required to publish your contact data in WHOIS. Likewise, Providers could be required to give your private contact details to anyone complaining that your website violates their trademark or copyright. None of these scenarios would require a court order, search warrant, or due process of any kind.

You can find out more about this here: http://www.savedomainprivacy.org/whats-changing/

You can do a couple of things:

  1. Give ICANN Feedback here: https://www.icann.org/public-comments/ppsai-initial-2015-05-05-en
  2. Sign the online petition: http://www.savedomainprivacy.org/sign-the-petition/

It's ambiguous in that it refers to a class of sports that are played on foot (as opposed to horseback, for example). There's not only soccer but American football and Australian Rules football, etc. The sport you are referring to as "football" is actually "association football".

I spent a good part of my childhood in England and as kids we mostly referred to it as soccer, even though in more formal terms it was referred to as football (like you'd probably say you play for your school's football team not soccer team, but when talking amongst ourselves we'd usually say hey let's play some soccer, not hey let's play some football).
It's called football because you play with your feet not because you play on foot. Unlike the other sports you mentioned.

You play with your whole body, not just your feet.

All the football sports: association football, gridiron football, Australian rules football, Gaelic football and rugby football involve use of the hands and feet on the ball.

Edit: I'll grant you this, Wikipedia states that there's no conclusive evidence for the etymology of the word football one way or the other:

There are conflicting explanations of the origin of the word "football". It is widely assumed that the word "football" (or "foot ball") references the action of the foot kicking a ball. There is an alternative explanation, which is that football originally referred to a variety of games in medieval Europe, which were played on foot.
